key_insight: Blackjack uses just two cfDNA fragmentation-similarity features to detect cancer with high accuracy in cross-validation, including early-stage disease.
clinical_relevance: This blood-based detection approach could support less invasive multi-cancer screening, but the study concerns cancer detection—not drug discovery—and does not establish clinical screening utility.
method: Encode DNA sequence context around plasma cfDNA fragmentation sites in position probability matrices.
Calculate similarity to reference matrices from healthy and cancer cohorts.
Use the two similarity features in logistic regression to classify samples.
evidence_signal: Cross-validation on two external whole-genome sequencing datasets yielded minimum AUC 0.993 and sensitivity 91.8% at 98% specificity overall; stage I sensitivity was 89.8% and stage II sensitivity was 90.2%.
watch_item: Prospective validation in representative screening populations is needed to determine real-world performance and clinical utility.
paper_title: Detection of early-stage cancer using similarity-based classification of cell-free DNA fragmentation patterns
